sections.title: Paywall Subscriptions — every setting
sections.excerpt: Paywall Subscriptions — every setting | The plan picker — how the subscription cards are arranged, where the selection checkbox sits, the plans themselves, the selected/unselected card styling and spacing, and each plan's name / price / note / billing-period labels, badge, and checkbox styling. This guide documents every setting of the Paywall Subscriptions block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Unselected plan style
sections.excerpt: Unselected plan style | How a plan card looks before the user taps it: background color, border, and spacing. Keep this neutral and understated so the chosen plan can clearly stand out against it. The contrast between this and the Selected style is what tells users which plan they've picked, so never make the two look the same.

sections.title: Space inside each plan card
sections.excerpt: Space inside each plan card | Sets the padding inside each plan card, between its labels and the card edge, on the top, bottom, left, and right. Increase it to make cards feel roomier and easier to tap, decrease it to fit more plans on screen. The theme default is usually fine; adjust only if cards look cramped in preview.

sections.title: Subscription plans
sections.excerpt: Subscription plans | The list of plans the user can buy. Each plan must be linked to a real product in your connected Stripe account, or checkout will fail when you publish. Per plan you set its four corner labels (top-left = plan name, bottom-left = description, top-right = price, bottom-right = billing period) and an optional badge. Mark your best-value plan as selected by default, since the pre-selected plan converts most often. Use 'Add Plan' to add rows.

sections.title: Plan name vs. price width
sections.excerpt: Plan name vs. price width | Sets how much of each plan card's width goes to the left labels (plan name and description), leaving the rest for the right labels (price and billing period). Around 60-70% usually gives names enough room while keeping prices aligned on the right. Lower it if prices look cramped, raise it if plan names wrap awkwardly.

sections.title: Plan badge
sections.excerpt: Plan badge | An optional ribbon on a plan card, like 'Most Popular' or 'Best Value', used to steer attention to the plan you most want sold. The styling (color, border, position, spacing) is shared across all plans, but the badge text is set per plan, so add text only to the one plan you're promoting. A single well-placed badge lifts conversion; badging every plan cancels the effect.

sections.title: Style the billing period (bottom-right)
sections.excerpt: Style the billing period (bottom-right) | Styles the bottom-right label on every plan card, usually the billing period like 'per month': font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. The text follows the linked product; this only sets the look. Keep it small and quiet under the price; theme defaults are a safe start.

sections.title: Style the plan note (bottom-left)
sections.excerpt: Style the plan note (bottom-left) | Styles the bottom-left label on every plan card, usually the short plan description or trial note: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. This sets only the look; you write the actual text per plan in the plan list. Keep it smaller and lighter than the plan name; theme defaults are a safe start.

sections.title: Style the plan checkbox
sections.excerpt: Style the plan checkbox | Sets the colors of the per-plan checkbox: its unselected (empty) color and its selected (checked) color. It only appears when checkbox placement is set to Left or Right, and is hidden when placement is 'No checkbox'. Use a clear, on-brand selected color so the chosen plan is unmistakable; it defaults to your theme accent.

sections.title: Style the price (top-right)
sections.excerpt: Style the price (top-right) | Styles the top-right label on every plan card, usually the price: font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. The price value itself comes from the linked Stripe product, not here. Make the price bold and prominent so it's easy to compare across plans; theme defaults usually work.

sections.title: Style the plan name (top-left)
sections.excerpt: Style the plan name (top-left) | Styles the top-left label on every plan card, which usually holds the plan name like 'Annual': font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing, applied to all plans at once. This only controls how it looks; you edit each plan's actual name in the plan list. Make plan names bold and legible so they're easy to compare; theme defaults usually work.

sections.title: Space around the plan list
sections.excerpt: Space around the plan list | Sets the space around the whole block of plans, between the list and the screen edges and the content above and below it. (Card padding spaces the inside of one plan; this spaces the entire group.) Add space if the plans feel jammed against the body copy or the purchase button; the theme default is a safe start.

sections.title: Checkbox placement on plans
sections.excerpt: Checkbox placement on plans | Choose where the selection checkbox sits on each plan card: left, right, or hidden. Left or right makes selecting a plan obvious; Hidden removes the checkbox and lets the highlighted card itself signal the choice for a cleaner look, but only if your selected style is clearly distinct. Left is a safe default. This also works together with the checkbox styling field below.

sections.title: Selected plan style
sections.excerpt: Selected plan style | How a plan card looks once it's the chosen one: background color, border, and spacing. Make it clearly stand out from the unselected cards, for example a brand-colored border or filled background, so the user is never unsure which plan they're about to buy. Crisp selected styling removes hesitation right before checkout.

sections.title: Plan card arrangement
sections.excerpt: Plan card arrangement | Choose how the plan cards are laid out. Vertical stacks them one under another, which reads best on mobile and works well for 2 to 4 plans; Horizontal lines them up side by side as compact cards, good for 2 short price options you want compared at a glance. Start with Vertical unless you specifically need a side-by-side comparison.
